business_problem: Atlassian wanted agents to do consequential work inside Jira, Confluence, and related products, but enterprise customers would only trust long-running automation if the models could follow complex instructions, use internal tools safely, and reason across huge contextual graphs.
solution_summary: Atlassian deploys Claude on Google Cloud behind the parts of its Rovo platform where the cost of a wrong answer is highest. Rovo Chat uses Claude as one of its base models to choose tools and skills across Jira, Confluence, and the rest of the suite, while Rovo Max takes a goal, pulls context from Teamwork Graph's billions of objects, and works in a managed environment where admins control packages and network access. The same Claude foundation powers Rovo CLI plus code review and generation flows that can read large repositories or pick up Jira tickets directly. Inside Atlassian, engineering runs heavily on Claude Code and recent pilots brought it to product managers and designers for small code changes and prototypes. This architecture lets Atlassian combine broad enterprise context, tool orchestration, and governed execution in one agent stack.

solution_components.name: Rovo Max
solution_components.role: Takes a goal rather than a single task and works until it reaches it under managed controls.

solution_components.name: Teamwork Graph
solution_components.role: Provides the connected context map of customer data that Rovo Max reasons over.

data_flow: A user goal or Jira/Confluence task enters Rovo Chat or Rovo Max, Claude selects tools and context from Teamwork Graph, works through the task in an admin-controlled environment, and returns actions, code, or artifacts back into Atlassian workflows where humans can keep collaborating.
business_outcome: Atlassian now runs more than 5 million agents in customer business workflows every month, serves millions of users on Rovo Chat, and uses Claude to automate increasingly complex work while keeping context and trust at the center of the platform.
